q1.answer: No, adr013 (node-fetch) is superseded by adr014. Adr014 says code running in Node.js should use the native fetch (Node.js 20+, undici-based, typed as `typeof fetch`), but frontend plugins and packages like this one should prefer the injected `fetchApiRef` (isomorphic packages accept an injected `typeof fetch` instead) — matching NotificationsClient's constructor-injected `fetchApi`.

q2.answer: ADR007 ('Use MSW to mock http requests') requires any `fetch`/`XMLHTTPRequest` in tests to be mocked with msw's express-style route handlers, as react-testing-library recommends, rather than each test mocking fetch/network requests its own ad-hoc way. This avoids (1) having to mock `fetch`/`XMLHTTPRequest` directly in each test, and (2) the inconsistency/duplication of every test inventing its own mocking implementation.

q3.answer: ADR006 cites two technical problems: React.FC implicitly adds a `children` prop, and it doesn't support generic types on children. The concrete upstream fact given is that Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript base template (via PR #8177) because it was deemed to have next to no benefit with these downsides.

q4.answer: ADR010 names Moment.js as the library luxon replaces, citing two reasons for its retirement: Moment.js causes large bundle sizes and has mutable-state issues (it is also being officially sunset by its own maintainers).

q5.answer: ADR004 ('Module Export Structure') requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way down to the package root `src/index.ts`. It was meant to make it easy to answer the question 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' (equivalently, 'what is exported from this directory?').

q6.answer: No — under ADR004's rule, a symbol is only publicly exported if it can be traced through an unbroken chain of index files up to `src/index.ts`. Since there is no `src/utils/index.ts` and `src/index.ts` never mentions these files, the chain is broken/non-existent, so `notificationLinks.ts` and `plainText.ts` are not part of the public API — the rule treats the absence of an index-file re-export as the marker of 'not exported', with no need for any explicit 'private' label.

q7.answer: ADR011 says `x-react` is for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a `notifications-react` package, its components/hooks (currently only consumed internally) would have to become something external frontend plugins need to depend on directly.

q8.answer: The one allowed exception is a default export for `React.lazy` modules. The workaround ADR003 offers to avoid even that is to wrap the lazy import manually, e.g. `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`, so the source module itself still only has named exports.

q9.answer: ADR015 ('Types and naming for element and component options') defines the `element`/`component` (synchronous) and `loader` (async/any) option patterns. Its Consequences section states the new pattern will be applied to the new frontend system's `@backstage/frontend-*` packages, but explicitly says existing APIs in the old frontend system's `@backstage/core-*` packages (the style the dev app predates/uses) will NOT be retrofitted.
